minutes.headline: Board backed the Hickory Hills dam easement, approved the NexAmp solar PILOT, and moved to pursue first refusal on 2030 Mass Ave
minutes.summary: The board heard presentations on the stormwater permit, retiree health liability, and the Hickory Hills dam easement. It then acted on the NexAmp solar PILOT, a common victualler license, and a Chapter 61B first-refusal parcel. It reviewed the draft November 28 special Town Meeting warrant without recommending any article, and discussed a road-opening moratorium notice and committee reports.

public_comment.topic: Citizen petition for a ten-year moratorium on selling municipal land and buildings (Save the Center).
Finance Committee public hearing on warrant articles on November 9.
Asked whether the Hickory Hills easement must go to Town Meeting.
Asked whether the solar PILOT shields the property from real estate tax increases.
Asked whether free cash already certified could be used at the special Town Meeting.
Reminded citizens the warrant is open until October 25 for citizen petitions.

votes.motion: Authorize Town Counsel, under the town manager's direction, to review and draft the proposed Hickory Hills easement.
Approve the NexAmp PILOT as presented, amended to be subject to calculations changing with the final project.
Approve the common victualler license for Global Montello Group at 134 Leominster Shirley Road.
Reopen the special Town Meeting warrant, closing October 25 at 5 p.m.
Pursue exercising the right of first refusal under Chapter 61B for 2030 Massachusetts Avenue.
Appoint Katie Childs to the Conservation Commission.

what_happened.line: The board voted to pursue the right of first refusal under Chapter 61B for 2030 Massachusetts Avenue.
The board voted to have Town Counsel review and draft the proposed Hickory Hills dam easement.
The board took up the NexAmp solar PILOT, a payment in place of taxes, with an amendment tying it to the final project; the minutes record the vote outcome as not audible.
The board reopened the special Town Meeting warrant, closing October 25 at 5 p.m., and reviewed draft articles without recommending any.
The board will not make warrant article recommendations next week and will revisit them later.

why_it_matters: The first-refusal vote and the solar payment arrangement could change what the town owns and what it collects, with the town budget, mostly taxes, bearing any purchase and appraisal cost.
Residents can still file citizen petitions for the November special Town Meeting until the warrant closes, and will be asked to vote on the articles there.
watch_next: Warrant closes October 25 at 5 p.m.; Finance Committee public hearing on warrant articles on November 9.
Town manager's report on the road opening moratorium notice and scheduling of a November building reuse workshop.
